title.zh: 从“技能执行者”转向“问题定义与验收者”
title.en: Shifting from Executor to Specifier & Quality Reviewer

old_assumption.zh: 个人职业护城河取决于自己亲手把活干得多快、工具用得多熟练。
old_assumption.en: Career moat depends on how fast and skillfully you execute tasks by hand.

new_shift.zh: 纯执行正在被 AI 快速廉价化，真正稀缺且高薪的能力正迅速向两端集中：精准写清需求规格（Spec）与一眼揪出隐蔽缺陷（Review）。
new_shift.en: Pure execution is rapidly commoditizing; high-value leverage now concentrates at two ends—writing razor-sharp specs and spotting subtle defects in AI output.

zh: 针对 [你的职业/岗位]，列出 5 个正在被 AI 迅速贬值的纯执行技能，以及 5 个因此变得更值钱的“定义问题/质量验收/责任兜底”类高杠杆能力。
帮我为 [你日常交付的一类核心产出，如 PRD/代码/营销方案] 设计一份“资深专家级验收清单（Review Rubric）”，让我从自己埋头写变成高效把关。
en: For [Your Role], list 5 pure execution skills rapidly losing market value to AI, and 5 high-leverage 'problem framing, taste, and quality review' skills rising in value.
Create a senior-level Review Rubric for [Core Deliverable You Produce] so I can shift from manual drafting to high-leverage specification and quality control.

note.zh: 工程界正从“手写每行代码”转向“维护高精度规格说明书与自动化测试”
note.en: Software engineering shifting from hand-coding toward high-precision specs and verification

title.zh: 用“2+1 技能组合”构造微型个人垄断
title.en: Building a Personal Micro-Monopoly via Skill Stacking

old_assumption.zh: 要在职场上胜出，必须在某一个单一赛道卷到全球前 1%。
old_assumption.en: To win in your career, you must grind into the top 1% of a single crowded discipline.

new_shift.zh: 单一维度卷前 1% 极难，但把两项前 20% 的常见技能加上一个独特行业语境交叉叠加，就能立刻在交叉点形成几乎没有竞争对手的微型垄断。
new_shift.en: Reaching top 1% in one skill is brutal—combining two top-20% skills with one specific domain context creates an almost competition-free micro-monopoly.

zh: 我目前具备的技能、经历和兴趣包括：[列出 3-5 个你的标签]。请帮我做交叉组合，找出 5 个我不需要和顶级专家硬碰硬、却能天然占据优势的“微型生态位”。
在我现有的核心能力 [技能 A] 之外，只需花 3 个月补齐哪一个“低门槛跨界技能 [技能 B]”，就能让我的稀缺度和议价能力翻倍？
en: My current skills, experiences, and interests are: [List 3-5 Traits]. Cross-combine them to identify 5 micro-monopoly niches where I have an unfair edge without fighting top-1% specialists.
Beside my core skill [Skill A], which adjacent skill could I learn to a solid top-20% level in 90 days to double my rarity and leverage?

note.zh: 经典“技能栈”模型：用多项前 25% 能力的组合击败单一维度的内卷
note.en: Classic talent-stack concept: combining multiple top-25% skills beats single-track grinding

title.zh: 用“前置作品证明”替代投递千篇一律的简历
title.en: Replacing Generic Resumes with Permissionless Proof-of-Work

old_assumption.zh: 找好机会、好客户或好工作，必须把简历投进招聘网站排队等 HR 筛选。
old_assumption.en: Landing great roles or clients means submitting a PDF resume into job portals and waiting.

new_shift.zh: AI 让投递成本归零后，HR 和甲方被海量完美简历淹没；直接针对目标团队的真实痛点做一个 2 小时的开源诊断或微型原型发过去，响应率高出一个数量级。
new_shift.en: AI flooded job boards with identical resumes—sending a 2-hour permissionless teardown or working mini-prototype for a target team's real problem cuts straight through the noise.

zh: 我想争取 [目标公司/目标客户类型] 的合作或岗位机会，我的强项是 [你的专长]。请帮我设计一个只需花半天时间就能做出的“免许可前置作品（Permissionless Proof-of-Work）”，以及一封 100 字以内不卑不亢的触达邮件。
把我的这段普通工作经历：[粘贴一段简历描述]，改造成一个让陌生人点开链接 30 秒就能看懂我实力的“可验证公开案例”。
en: I want to reach [Target Company/Client Type] using my strength in [Your Skill]. Design a half-day permissionless proof-of-work project I can build for them, plus a concise 100-word outreach message.
Turn this dry resume bullet—[Paste Bullet]—into a verifiable public case study a stranger can evaluate in 30 seconds.

note.zh: 不等对方给职位，先免费交付高质量可视化作品赢得顶级合作机会
note.en: Delivering unsolicited high-value work upfront to earn high-trust opportunities

title.zh: 写一份“个人协作说明书”，减少隐性沟通摩擦
title.en: Writing a Personal Operating Manual to Cut Collaboration Friction

old_assumption.zh: 合作默契只能靠相处久了慢慢猜，把偏好和边界写出来显得生硬。
old_assumption.en: Working alignment happens naturally over time; stating preferences upfront feels stiff.

new_shift.zh: 多数协作摩擦源于默认规则不同——一份坦诚、简洁的个人协作说明，能提前省掉大量猜忌与返工。
new_shift.en: Much collaboration friction comes from unspoken defaults—a short, candid guide to how you work prevents guesswork and rework.

zh: 根据我的工作习惯：[简述你的作息/沟通偏好/擅长与短板]，帮我起草一份 300 字左右的“个人协作说明书”，涵盖高效沟通方式、深度工作时段和协作红线。
在我过往的团队或项目合作中，最常出现的误会是：[描述常见误会]。请帮我写 2 条清晰、不生硬的协作约定放进自我介绍或开工对齐里。
en: Based on how I work—[Briefly Describe Schedule, Comms Style, Strengths & Quirks]—draft a concise personal operating manual covering communication, deep work blocks, and boundaries.
A recurring misunderstanding in my collaborations is: [Describe Friction]. Write 2 clear, natural working agreements I can share upfront when kicking off projects.

note.zh: 许多高绩效团队流行公开个人 README，用显性规则替代隐性猜测
note.en: Personal READMEs replace guesswork with clear expectations in modern teams

title.zh: 把“做过一次的复杂事”沉淀成可复用手册，而不是每次重头干
title.en: Turning One-Off Hard Tasks into Reusable Playbooks

old_assumption.zh: 事情做完了就算翻篇，下次遇到类似任务再临时想办法、重新摸索。
old_assumption.en: Once a task is done, move on—figure it out again next time similar work comes up.

new_shift.zh: 把踩坑经验、检查清单和 AI 提示词固化成一份结构化 Playbook 后，下次同类任务启动速度会快 5 倍，还能直接复用给他人或 Agent。
new_shift.en: Packaging hard-won steps, checklists, and prompts into a playbook makes the next run 5x faster and gives you a reusable asset for teammates or agents.

zh: 我最近刚完成一件比较复杂的任务：[描述任务与踩过的坑]。请帮我把它整理成一份可复用的标准操作手册（Playbook），包含前置准备、执行步骤、常见陷阱和验收标准。
盘点我过去一个月里重复做过至少两次的 [某类工作任务]，挑出最值得沉淀成模板/清单的 2 项，给出最小骨架。
en: I recently finished a complex task: [Describe Task & Pitfalls]. Turn it into a reusable playbook with prep steps, execution order, common traps, and a done checklist.
Look across [Type of Work] I did more than once last month—pick the 2 best candidates to turn into reusable playbooks and outline their minimal structure.

note.zh: 把隐性经验显性化为可复用剧本，是摆脱低效重复劳动的关键一步
note.en: Turning tacit know-how into repeatable playbooks eliminates ground-zero restarts

title.zh: 按“精力曲线”排程，而不是按“日历格子”硬塞任务
title.en: Scheduling Around Energy Curves Instead of Packing Calendar Slots

old_assumption.zh: 只要把待办事项塞进日历的空白时间段，一天就算安排好了。
old_assumption.en: A good day is simply filling open calendar blocks with to-do items.

new_shift.zh: 不同时间段人的认知带宽与精力质量差异巨大；把高创造力/高决策任务放在精力峰值，把低认知琐事留给低谷，同样工时产出完全不同。
new_shift.en: Cognitive sharpness fluctuates across the day—matching high-judgment work to peak energy and low-friction chores to troughs changes output without adding hours.

zh: 我一天中精力最清醒、最适合深度思考的时段是：[填时段]，最容易犯困或走神的是：[填时段]。请帮我把 [你的核心任务与日常琐事] 按精力高低重新匹配排程。
当我下午或晚上精力明显下滑时，有哪些“低脑力消耗但有推进感”的收尾任务可以替代硬啃难题？
en: My peak focus window is [Peak Hours] and my energy dips around [Low Hours]. Re-map my [Core Tasks & Routine Chores] so deep thinking hits peak energy.
When my energy drops later in the day, what low-cognitive-load tasks still move things forward without forcing hard problem-solving?

note.zh: 时间与节律研究表明，任务类型与生理/认知节律的匹配度直接影响表现
note.en: Research on timing shows matching analytical and creative work to daily energy rhythms improves outcomes

title.zh: 靠“低成本小实验组合”攒职业期权，而不是把筹码全押在一处
title.en: Building Career Optionality Through Small Low-Cost Bets

old_assumption.zh: 精力有限，只能死守一条主线，做点小实验就是“不务正业、分散注意力”。
old_assumption.en: With limited bandwidth, you must stay 100% locked on one track—small experiments feel like a distraction.

new_shift.zh: 单点押注在环境突变时很脆弱；用少量业余时间跑低成本、可复用的小项目或小研究，既能反哺主业，又能悄悄攒出备选路径和真实作品。
new_shift.en: Single-track bets carry fragility when markets shift; small, low-cost experiments build real proof of work and optionality without betting the farm.

zh: 结合我目前的主业/方向：[简述现状] 和每周最多可投入的 [如 3-5 小时] 时间，设计 2 个“低成本、能反哺主业又积累长期资产”的微型探索方向。
如何判断一个副线实验该“继续加码”还是“果断止损关掉”，帮我定一套简单客观的退出标准。
en: Given my current track [Briefly Describe] and up to [e.g. 3-5] hours a week, propose 2 low-cost experiments that reinforce my main work while building long-term assets.
Help me set clear, objective stop-or-double-down criteria so side experiments don't become endless guilt or drift.

note.zh: 保留多条低成本选项能显著提升面对不确定性时的抗脆弱能力
note.en: Maintaining low-cost options increases resilience when external conditions change

title.zh: 在开工前把“验收标准与预期”说透，而不是做完再返工
title.en: Aligning on 'Done' Criteria Upfront Instead of Reworking at the End

old_assumption.zh: 任务接过来先埋头做完再交差，做出来不合意再改，这叫“能干、不挑活”。
old_assumption.en: Take the task, grind it out, present the finished result, and revise if someone asks for changes.

new_shift.zh: 很多加班和返工源于一开始对“什么算做好”没有对齐；花 5 分钟确认核心目标、边界和样例标准，往往能省掉后面 5 轮修改。
new_shift.en: Much late-stage rework comes from unaligned definitions of 'done'—spending 5 minutes upfront confirming goals, scope, and examples saves rounds of revision.

zh: 我即将开始一项 [项目/任务/合作]：[简述任务]。请帮我列出一份“开工 5 分钟对齐清单”，帮我把模糊要求变成可验收的具体标准。
当上级或合作方给的需求很模糊、甚至前后矛盾时，帮我写一套温和但清晰的“澄清与确认话术”，既不显得顶撞又能把边界定准。
en: I'm about to start [Project/Task/Collaboration]: [Brief Summary]. Give me a 5-minute kickoff checklist to turn vague asks into clear acceptance criteria.
When a request is fuzzy or shifting, write calm, constructive clarifying questions that lock down scope and 'done' criteria early.

note.zh: 明确边界与“完成定义”能大幅减少中途改向与无效返工
note.en: Clear boundaries and appetite/done definitions prevent mid-stream thrash and rework

title.zh: 用“教别人 / 写给新手看”来检验自己是不是真懂
title.en: Testing True Mastery by Explaining Clearly to Beginners

old_assumption.zh: 看懂了概念、收藏了资料，就等于自己已经掌握了这项能力。
old_assumption.en: Reading explanations and saving bookmarks means you've mastered the topic.

new_shift.zh: 一讲给外行或写进教程就卡壳的地方，正是你理解最虚的盲区；把学到的东西用大白话讲清楚，既能补漏洞又能留下公开资产。
new_shift.en: Where you stumble explaining a concept plainly to a beginner is where your understanding has gaps—teaching exposes blindspots and creates shareable assets.

zh: 我最近在学 [某个新概念/新工具/新方法]：[简述你的理解]。请扮演一位好奇但没有背景的新手，向我提 4 个最容易暴露理解漏洞的“为什么/如果……会怎样”问题。
帮我把我对 [某项技能或概念] 的理解，改写成一段没有黑话、带生活类比的 150 字通俗解释。
en: I've been learning [Concept/Tool/Method]: [Summarize Your Understanding]. Act as a curious beginner and ask 4 probing questions that expose any fuzzy spots in my grasp.
Rewrite my explanation of [Concept/Skill] in plain, jargon-free language with a relatable everyday analogy.

note.zh: 用通俗语言复述与教学是检验真懂与发现认知盲区的高效方法
note.en: Explaining ideas simply is a sharp test of real understanding and hidden gaps

title.zh: 靠“说话算话与靠谱交付”积累信任复利，而不是刷存在感
title.en: Compounding Trust Through Reliable Follow-Through Over Loud Networking

old_assumption.zh: 拓展人脉和职业机会，靠的是多加好友、多参加社交场合或频繁客套。
old_assumption.en: Growing opportunities means collecting contacts, attending events, and staying visible everywhere.

new_shift.zh: 在信息噪音越来越大的环境里，“答应的事按时做到、遇到坑提前说清、不制造额外麻烦”的稀缺度极高，会带来长期、低摩擦的回头合作。
new_shift.en: In noisy environments, reliability—following through, flagging risks early, and making others' lives easier—compounds into high-trust, repeat collaborations.

zh: 审视我目前正在推进的几项合作或承诺：[简述现状]，帮我检查有没有哪件事进度滞后却还没主动同步，设计一句真诚、不推卸的提前沟通话术。
结合 [你的工作或合作场景]，列出 3 个看似很小、但最能让合作方觉得“这人特别靠谱、愿意长期合作”的日常细节。
en: Check my current commitments or collaborations—[Brief Summary]—and draft a transparent, proactive update for anything running behind or hitting a snag.
In [Your Work or Collaboration Context], list 3 small habits that signal high reliability and make people eager to work with you again.

note.zh: 长期主义合作中，可预测性与诚信往往比短期曝光更能带来优质机会
note.en: Predictability and follow-through often unlock stronger opportunities over time than surface visibility

title.zh: 提“带背景和尝试过什么”的问题，拿到 10 倍有用的回答
title.en: Asking Context-Rich Questions That Earn High-Signal Answers

old_assumption.zh: 向别人或 AI 请教时，丢一句“怎么办”或“帮我看看这个”，对方自然会给完整答案。
old_assumption.en: Asking 'what should I do?' or pasting a raw link without context is enough to get a great answer.

new_shift.zh: 把“目标、已有上下文、已经试过的做法、具体卡点”讲清楚，别人和 AI 都能跳过废话直接给干货，请教成本和对方负担都会大幅降低。
new_shift.en: Sharing goal, context, what you already tried, and the exact blocker skips generic fluff and makes it easy for busy people or AI to give sharp help.

zh: 我想向 [某位资深同行/导师/专家] 请教 [某个具体问题]：[简述你的问题与现状]。请帮我整理一段 120 字以内、重点突出、尊重对方时间的请教消息。
把下面这段我准备发出去的求助/提问：[粘贴提问]，改写成结构更清晰、更容易被快速回答的版本。
en: I want to ask [Experienced Peer or Mentor] about [Specific Problem]: [Context & What I Tried]. Draft a respectful, concise message under 120 words that makes it easy to answer.
Tighten this help request—[Paste Draft]—so the context, blocker, and specific ask stand out at a glance.

note.zh: 清晰的上下文与明确的问题边界，是获得高质量协助的最强加速器
note.en: Clear context and specific blockers consistently unlock better answers from peers and tools

title.zh: 用“两周刻意冲刺 + 真实作品”练技能，而不是漫无目的看课
title.en: Running a 2-Week Skill Sprint Around a Real Output Instead of Passive Courses

old_assumption.zh: 学一项新技能应该先把整套课程、长教程或厚书刷完，再考虑动手做东西。
old_assumption.en: Learning a new skill means finishing full courses, tutorials, or books before making something real.

new_shift.zh: 光看课很容易产生“学会了”的错觉；定一个两周小目标，围绕一个真实小作品边做边查、边改边练，掌握速度通常会快得多。
new_shift.en: Passive watching creates an illusion of competence—a 2-week sprint anchored to a small real output builds practical skill much faster.

zh: 我想在接下来两周里快速上手 [某项具体技能/工具]：[简述你的基础与目标]。请帮我设计一个“以做出 1 个小作品/完成 1 个真实任务为终点”的两周冲刺计划。
针对 [你想练的技能]，帮我列出最核心的 20% 基础知识和最容易踩的 3 个新手坑，让我跳过冗余内容直接动手。
en: I want to build working momentum in [Skill or Tool] over the next 2 weeks: [Background & Goal]. Design a hands-on sprint centered on one small real deliverable.
For [Skill], highlight the core 20% fundamentals to learn first and 3 common beginner traps so I can start building right away.

note.zh: 围绕真实问题与作品倒逼学习，能让零散知识点真正连成可用能力
note.en: Learning anchored to a concrete deliverable turns scattered notes into usable skill

title.zh: 做“跨语言翻译器”，把技术/专业细节翻成对方关心的结果
title.en: Translating Technical & Domain Details into What Stakeholders Care About

old_assumption.zh: 把底层实现细节、专业术语和复杂过程讲得越全，别人越能理解你的工作价值。
old_assumption.en: Explaining every technical detail, jargon term, and internal step proves the value of your work.

new_shift.zh: 不同角色关心的语言完全不同——业务方看结果与风险，协作者看接口与节点；能把专业动作翻译成对方听得懂、用得上的表达，沟通效率会翻倍。
new_shift.en: Different stakeholders care about different outcomes and risks—translating domain work into their language cuts friction and gets faster alignment.

zh: 我最近做了一项 [技术/分析/设计/运营] 工作：[简述你做了什么与核心价值]。请帮我分别写成给“业务/决策方看（重结果与影响）”和给“协作伙伴看（重配合与边界）”的两个简短版本。
在 [你的工作场景] 中，哪些专业术语或内部细节最容易让非同背景的人听不懂？帮我改写成大白话。
en: I recently worked on [Technical, Analytical, Design, or Ops Work]: [Summary & Impact]. Write two concise updates—one for decision-makers (outcomes/risks) and one for collaborators (handoffs/next steps).
Which jargon or internal details in [Your Role] tend to confuse non-specialists, and how can I phrase them plainly?

note.zh: 根据受众关切点调整表达重点，是跨职能推进中最实用也最常被低估的能力
note.en: Tailoring updates to what each audience cares about speeds up alignment across roles

title.zh: 每做完一个拿得出手的项目，顺手留一份“脱敏复盘样本”
title.en: Saving a Clean Case Study After Every Meaningful Project

old_assumption.zh: 等以后要跳槽、接单或做分享时，再临时翻旧文件、拼凑案例。
old_assumption.en: Wait until you need a job application, client pitch, or talk to dig through old files and piece together examples.

new_shift.zh: 隔半年再回忆细节会丢掉很多关键判断；做完就花 20 分钟记下“背景、卡点、你的做法、结果与反思”，日积月累就是最硬的个人履历。
new_shift.en: Details fade fast—spending 20 minutes right after finishing a project to record problem, approach, trade-offs, and outcome builds real proof over time.

zh: 我刚结束或阶段性完成了一件事：[简述项目、你的角色与结果]。请帮我套用“背景 → 卡点 → 做法与取舍 → 结果与复盘”四段式，整理成一份清晰的个人案例记录。
帮我设计一套极简的“项目结项 20 分钟复盘模板”，让我以后每次做完重要任务都能顺手留档。
en: I just wrapped up [Project or Milestone]: [Brief Context, My Role & Outcome]. Structure a clean case note covering context, bottleneck, approach/trade-offs, and result.
Design a lightweight 20-minute project wrap-up template so I capture real examples while details are still fresh.

note.zh: 真实问题拆解与取舍过程，往往比干巴巴的头衔和技能词更有说服力
note.en: Real problem framing and trade-offs speak louder than job titles or buzzword lists

title.zh: 在“粗糙草稿阶段”就要反馈，而不是等打磨到完美才拿出来
title.en: Asking for Feedback on Rough Drafts Before Over-Polishing

old_assumption.zh: 东西做得够完整、够体面了再给人看，拿半成品出来显得不成熟。
old_assumption.en: Share work only after it looks polished and complete—showing a rough draft feels premature.

new_shift.zh: 方向偏了时，早期粗稿改起来几乎不疼；等全部做完再改，往往整块推倒重来。越早拿模糊草稿对准方向，越少走冤枉路。
new_shift.en: Early rough drafts are cheap to steer; late-stage revisions often mean throwing away finished work—checking direction early saves big rework.

zh: 我刚搭了一个 [方案/草稿/原型/思路] 的雏形：[简述雏形与想确认的点]。请帮我写一段简短话术，向 [合作方/同事/同行] 请教“方向和结构有没有跑偏”，而不是扣字眼。
在 [你的日常工作或创作流程] 中，哪一步最适合提前 30% 拿出来做一次快速对齐？
en: I have a rough early draft of [Plan, Doc, or Prototype]: [Brief Summary & What I Want Checked]. Write a short note asking for direction/structure feedback rather than minor polish.
In [Your Work or Creative Process], where would a 30%-done check-in catch misalignment before heavy effort goes in?

note.zh: 在低成本阶段对齐方向与边界，能显著减少后期大规模返工
note.en: Aligning on direction early while changes are cheap prevents heavy rework later

title.zh: 把碎片时间留给琐事，给难啃的硬活留整块安静时间
title.en: Matching Deep Work to Unbroken Blocks and Chores to Fragments

old_assumption.zh: 只要有空档就随时插空做复杂任务，零碎时间也能把硬活一点点拼完。
old_assumption.en: Any free 15-minute gap is enough to chip away at complex thinking or creative tasks.

new_shift.zh: 复杂思考需要进入状态和上下文加载，频繁被打断会让脑子一直处于“重启加载”中；把整块时间留给硬活，零碎时间处理回消息、整理和收尾。
new_shift.en: Deep work requires loading context and staying unbroken—reserving uninterrupted blocks for hard problems and using gaps for quick chores cuts switching cost.

zh: 我这周需要推进的硬活是：[填核心任务]，日常琐碎事务包括：[填零碎事务]。请帮我设计一种简单的日程安排方式，把整块时间留给核心任务。
当我在做深度工作时，最容易被哪 2 种外部或内部干扰打断？给出简单可行的隔离办法。
en: This week I need deep progress on [Hard Task] alongside smaller chores like [Small Chores]. Sketch a simple way to protect uninterrupted blocks for the hard work.
What 2 interruptions pull me out of focus most often, and what low-friction rule helps keep those blocks intact?

note.zh: 减少上下文切换、保护连续思考时间，是做出高质量产出的关键前提
note.en: Reducing context switches and protecting unbroken time makes deep thinking far more effective

title.zh: 建一份“个人踩坑与误判账本”，让同一类坑只踩一次
title.en: Keeping a Personal Mistake & Misjudgment Ledger So You Pay Once

old_assumption.zh: 犯错或判断失误后尽快翻篇、别老盯着不愉快的事看，下次自然会记住。
old_assumption.en: After a mistake or bad call, move on quickly and don't dwell on it—you'll remember next time.

new_shift.zh: 记性靠不住，相似的坑换个马甲还会再来；花 3 分钟记下“当时为什么这么判 + 信号是什么 + 下次前置检查点”，每次犯错都在升级你的过滤网。
new_shift.en: Memory fades when similar traps return in disguise—logging why a call went wrong and one pre-check turns mistakes into durable filters.

zh: 回想我过去半年在 [工作/项目/决策/表达] 中踩过的 3 个印象最深的坑：[简述 3 次经历]。帮我提炼出每一种坑的“早期预警信号”和一条“下次开工前自检问题”。
帮我设计一份 3 分钟就能填完的“个人误判/踩坑记录模板”，重点留住教训而不是自我责备。
en: Looking back at 3 costly mistakes or misjudgments in [Work, Projects, Decisions, or Comms]: [Briefly Describe 3 Cases]. Extract an early warning sign and one pre-action check for each.
Design a 3-minute mistake log focused on learning and prevention rather than self-blame.

note.zh: 把失误写成冷静的因果与预防清单，能把一次性代价变成长期护栏
note.en: Turning setbacks into calm causal notes and check rules converts one-off costs into lasting guardrails
